title: Swedish Housing Law Logical Universe
purpose: Declared, source-attributed legal universe for a specialized QCDS Legal Logical Robot. The corpus models applicability, temporal transitions and a bounded set of operational housing-law consequences without modifying QCDS core semantics.

sources.title: Lag (2012:978) om uthyrning av egen bostad

sections.summary: Applies to compensated residential letting by a natural person or estate, subject to exclusions.
Excludes regular letting of more than two external units, units held with tenancy right, and holiday-purpose letting.
Terms less favorable to the tenant are without effect unless the Act provides otherwise.
Agreement is indefinite unless a fixed term is agreed.
Rent is agreed as a fixed amount, with bounded utility-cost exceptions.
Tenant may seek rent review; substantially higher rent than comparable private lettings may be reduced.
Tenant may terminate immediately for a material defect not promptly remedied after notice.
Independent second-hand letting requires landlord consent.
Lodgers may not be accommodated beyond what the landlord reasonably must accept; consent is required when the unit is part of the landlord's home.
Fixed-term agreement ends at term; tenant may always terminate with three-month notice to a month-end.
Indefinite agreement may be terminated with three-month notice to a month-end.
Landlord may terminate immediately when rent is more than two weeks late, subject to cure rules.
Unauthorized transfer, independent sublet or specified lodger breach may support immediate termination when no valid excuse exists.
For specified grounds including late rent, timely cure before termination removes that termination ground.
Act enters into force 1 July 2026, repeals 2012:978, while the old Act remains applicable to agreements entered under it.
Legacy Act applied to qualifying private residential letting outside business; tenancy sublets excluded; only first letting covered; Chapter 12 JB applied residually.
Terms less favorable to tenant are without effect unless otherwise provided.
Tenant notice is one month, landlord notice three months, and tenant has no extension right unless agreed.
Rent review uses capital and operating cost framework, bounded by the agreed rent.
Act entered into force 1 February 2013; earlier agreements remained under Chapter 12 JB.
Chapter 12 contains the general Swedish tenancy regime and remains the baseline where special private-letting legislation does not displace it.
General Chapter 12 rent rules govern when the special private-letting rent regime is not applicable.
2026 amendments to Chapter 12 entered into force 1 July 2026 with specified transition rules.

rules.explanation: The 2026 private-letting Act applies because the positive scope requirements are met and the modeled exclusions are explicitly absent.
Regular letting of more than two external units is outside the 2026 Act; the case falls back to the general tenancy-law track modeled here.
A landlord who holds the unit with tenancy right is outside the 2026 Act.
Holiday-purpose letting is outside the 2026 Act. The robot does not force Chapter 12 applicability without a separate scope check.
A qualifying agreement entered before 1 July 2026 remains governed by the repealed 2012 Act under the 2026 transition rule, with Chapter 12 JB residual application.
The legacy Act only covered the first letting when multiple units were let.
The legacy Act did not apply to second-hand letting of a tenancy right.
The legacy Act required letting outside business activity.
Agreements entered before the 2012 Act took effect remained under Chapter 12 JB.
A modeled contractual term that is less favorable to the tenant is ineffective against the tenant unless the Act permits the deviation.
The legacy Act likewise made less favorable tenant terms ineffective unless otherwise allowed.
Rent more than two weeks late can support immediate termination when the modeled cure condition has not occurred before termination.
When the tenant cures before termination on the specified late-rent ground, that ground no longer supports termination.
Independent second-hand use requires landlord consent.
Unauthorized independent subletting can support immediate termination when no valid excuse is shown.
Fixed term ends at the agreed end, while tenant retains a three-month termination route to a month-end.
Indefinite agreements use the Act's three-month notice route to a month-end.
Legacy private-letting contracts used one-month tenant notice, three-month landlord notice, and no statutory extension right unless agreed.
The 2026 Act's modeled rent-review path compares with similar private lettings and can reduce a substantially higher rent.
The legacy rent-review framework used capital and operating costs, bounded by the agreed rent.
When the general tenancy regime controls, Chapter 12 JB supplies the rent-review framework.
A material defect not promptly remedied after notice can support immediate tenant termination.
